terrarium.help.title: OBSERVATION GUIDE
terrarium.help.intro: Each ant observes its surroundings and decides whether to explore, collect, follow pheromones, flee or return to the nest. Interactions shape the colony's behavior.
terrarium.help.lifecycle.title: The life cycle
terrarium.help.lifecycle: A new terrarium starts with two alates and intact soil. Favorable humidity and light after rain allow flight. The queen mates, sheds her wings, digs and raises the first nanitics using maternal reserves, without foraging. Workers must then forage. Times are accelerated; this is not a biological calendar.
terrarium.help.colonies.title: New colonies
terrarium.help.colonies: Mature colonies can reserve food for princesses and males. Alates must leave the nest and find a warm, humid window after rain. A daughter queen founds another shelter with her own resources and lineage. If they miss the window, they may need more rain. Current limit: four colonies per experiment.
terrarium.help.replay.title: Repeat and compare
terrarium.help.replay: The same seed, conditions and sequence of interventions reproduce a run. “Replay” reapplies interventions at the same times. Scenario B starts from the current state with one additional humidity point.
terrarium.help.forecast.title: Forecast with uncertainty
terrarium.help.forecast: The forecast runs 18 scenarios with small light and humidity variations and new random choices. The interval shows the 10th–90th percentiles of those simulations, not a guarantee. Compare forecasts with outcomes.
terrarium.help.limits: Randomness and chaos are different concepts. Divergence between scenarios alone does not prove mathematical chaos. This prototype explores a simplified ecological model; its results do not validate forecasts for a real terrarium. Limit: 450 ants and brood.
